title: BIZRA Capability Negotiation Contract v1.0
description: Defines how nodes declare capabilities, how missions request capabilities, and how the URP mediates between unequal hardware to enforce equal citizenship.

node_capability_card.description: What a node declares it can do. Sent to URP on connect and refreshed periodically.

capabilities.description: What this node can do — derived from installed models, tools, AND physical sensors

tier.description: Self-declared capability tier. URP uses this for routing.

device_role.description: Role in the user's personal sovereign cluster

cluster_peer_ids.description: Other devices belonging to same human identity. Enables cross-device offload.

models.description: Models this node has installed and can run locally

max_latency_class.description: Slowest latency class this node can serve

mission_capability_request.description: What a mission asks for — capabilities, not models. This is the contract-first principle.

required_capabilities.description: What the mission needs (e.g. ['chat', 'memory_retrieval']). NEVER a model name.

evidence_standard.description: What evidence the mission must produce

requires_urp_validation.description: If true, output must pass through URP SAT before entering network

urp_mediation_result.description: The URP's decision after comparing node capability vs mission requirement. This is the equalizer.

verdict.description: local_sufficient: node can handle alone. local_with_urp_enrichment: node executes, URP enriches. urp_assisted: URP provides compute help. urp_delegated: URP handles entirely. rejected: below constitutional minimum.

local_model.description: Model to use locally (null if URP handles)

urp_model.description: Model URP will use for enrichment (null if not needed)

ihsan_floor_override.description: URP may lower the Ihsan floor for weaker nodes (never below 0.85)

constitutional_rules.description: Hard rules the URP enforces. These protect the 8B-human mission.

rule_1_no_model_lock_in.const: No mission contract may require a specific model family. Missions specify capabilities, never vendor/model names.

rule_2_urp_before_network.const: Every node connects to URP first, then to the network. No direct node-to-node traffic for mission results.

rule_3_receipt_required.const: No output enters the network without a constitutional receipt. URP SAT validates all receipts.

rule_4_equal_law.const: Constitutional gates (Ihsan, SNR, Guardian) apply identically to all nodes. Hardware differences affect execution quality, never governance rules.

rule_5_degradation_over_silence.const: A weaker node that produces honest degraded output is always preferred over a stronger node that produces unverifiable output.

rule_6_urp_enrichment_is_aid_not_replace.const: URP enrichment enhances local output. It never replaces the local node's receipt or claim of authorship. The local PAT remains the author.

rule_7_minimum_ihsan_is_universal.const: The Ihsan floor (0.85 minimum, 0.95 target) applies to every node equally. URP enrichment exists to help weaker nodes reach the floor, not to exempt them from it.
